# 1 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The king of Egypt began mobilizing — a massive army, countless as sand on a beach, and a large fleet — because he was scheming to swallow Alexander's kingdom whole.

**2** He marched into Syria wearing a smile, and the cities opened their gates to him with welcomes, because Alexander had told them to — Ptolemy was his father-in-law, after all.

**3** But in every city he entered, Ptolemy quietly installed a garrison.

**4** When he reached Azotus, his hosts made a point of showing him what Jonathan had done — the ruins of Dagon's temple, the burned-out city, the bodies piled along the road from the previous campaign.

**5** They told the king the whole story, hoping to get Jonathan in trouble. The king said nothing.

**6** Jonathan met Ptolemy at Joppa with full ceremony. They exchanged pleasantries and spent the night there.

**7** Jonathan traveled with the king as far as the Eleutherus River, then headed back to Jerusalem.

**8** By this point Ptolemy had grabbed all the coastal cities as far north as Seleucia-by-the-Sea. And behind Alexander's back, he was already plotting to take everything.

**9** He sent word to Demetrius: "Let's make a deal. I'll give you my daughter — the one I gave Alexander — and you can have your father's kingdom back.

**10** I regret ever handing her to Alexander. He tried to have me killed."

**11** It was a lie, of course. Ptolemy wanted the kingdom for himself.

**12** He took his daughter back from Alexander and gave her to Demetrius. His split with Alexander was now in the open.

**13** Ptolemy walked into Antioch and put on the crown of Asia. He now wore two crowns: Egypt's and Asia's.

**14** Alexander happened to be in Cilicia at the time, suppressing a local revolt.

**15** He rushed back to fight Ptolemy. Ptolemy met him with overwhelming force and crushed him.

**16** Alexander escaped to Arabia, looking for refuge. Ptolemy stood triumphant.

**17** Then an Arab chief named Zabdiel cut off Alexander's head and sent it to Ptolemy.

**18** Ptolemy himself died three days later. The fortresses fell to their own garrisons.

**19** Demetrius II took the throne in 145 BCE.

**20** During this period, Jonathan mobilized Judea's forces to attack the Jerusalem citadel, building a full siege train against it.

**21** Some Jewish traitors who hated their own people rushed to the new king with the news: Jonathan was besieging the citadel.

**22** Demetrius was furious. He immediately traveled to Ptolemais and sent Jonathan an ultimatum: lift the siege and come to me at once.

**23** Jonathan's response: keep the siege going. Then he handpicked some elders and priests, took a political risk, and went to meet the king anyway.

**24** He brought silver, gold, fine clothing, and expensive gifts and came before Demetrius at Ptolemais. He won the king over.

**25** The same renegades who had been trying to destroy him lodged their accusations again —

**26** but the king treated Jonathan exactly as his predecessors had. He honored him publicly before all his courtiers,

**27** confirmed him as high priest with all his previous honors, and formally registered him among the king's chief friends, first rank.

**28** Jonathan pressed his advantage and asked the king to free Judea from tribute and to incorporate the three Samaritan districts, pledging three hundred talents of silver in return.

**29** The king agreed and drew up official letters to that effect:

**30** "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

**31** Enclosed is a copy of the letter we sent to our kinsman Lasthenes concerning you, for your information.

**32** King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.

**33** We have determined to show favor to the Jewish people, our friends, who have kept faith with us, in recognition of their loyalty.

**34** We hereby confirm to them the territory of Judea plus the three districts of Aphaerema, Lydda, and Ramathaim — annexed from Samaria with all their dependencies — in lieu of the annual royal revenues previously collected from the land and its orchards.

**35** We also release them from all other obligations due to us: tithes, customs duties, salt revenues, and crown taxes — all cancelled.

**36** These provisions are permanent and irrevocable.

**37** Please ensure that a copy of this document is given to Jonathan and publicly displayed on the holy mountain."

**38** Now that the land was calm and he faced no opposition, Demetrius sent home almost all his troops — every man to his homeland — keeping only the foreign mercenaries from overseas. This made him universally hated among the veterans of his father's army.

**39** A man named Trypho, one of Alexander's old supporters, watched all this discontent building and saw an opportunity. He went to an Arab chieftain named Imalkue, who was raising Antiochus — Alexander's young son —

**40** and he said: "Give me the boy. He should be king in his father's place." He laid out the whole case: what Demetrius had done, how much the troops despised him. He stayed there a long time, building support.

**41** Jonathan also sent a formal request to Demetrius: withdraw the citadel garrison from Jerusalem, and pull the troops from the other Judean strongholds — they'd been harassing Israel constantly.

**42** Demetrius wrote back: "I'll do more than that for you and your people — I'll honor you greatly as soon as I have the chance.

**43** For right now, do me this one favor: send me fighting men. My whole army has mutinied."

**44** Jonathan dispatched three thousand crack troops to Antioch. They arrived to the king's immense relief.

**45** But the city itself had turned against Demetrius. About a hundred and twenty thousand civilians rose up and tried to kill him.

**46** The king fled into the palace. The mob took the streets and began the assault.

**47** The king called on the Jews for help. They poured into the city and spread out through every quarter, killing as they went. About a hundred thousand men died that day.

**48** They burned sections of the city, looted heavily, and saved the king's life.

**49** When the citizens of Antioch realized the Jews had the city in an iron grip, they lost heart completely and came crying to the king:

**50** "Make them stop. Give us terms. Make peace — we surrender."

**51** The king stood down and negotiated peace. The Jews came out of it with enormous prestige throughout the kingdom, and returned to Jerusalem laden with plunder.

**52** Demetrius II was now settled on his throne, and the land was at peace.

**53** Then he broke every promise. He cut Jonathan off completely, refused to honor his commitments, and treated him with hostility.

**54** This opened the door for Trypho. He returned with young Antiochus, crowned him king, and gave him the diadem.

**55** Every soldier Demetrius had dismissed flocked to Antiochus. Demetrius was defeated and fled.

**56** Trypho captured the elephants and held Antioch.

**57** Young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan: "I confirm you as high priest. I am appointing you over the four districts. You are named one of the king's friends."

**58** He sent golden dishes and a full table service, the right to drink from gold cups, wear purple, and display a golden brooch.

**59** He appointed Jonathan's brother Simon as governor of everything from the Ladder of Tyre to Egypt's border.

**60** Jonathan made a tour of the Trans-Euphrates cities and all the Syrian forces came to his side. He came to Ashkelon and received a warm reception.

**61** He headed for Gaza next, but Gaza slammed the gates. He put the city under siege, burned the outlying towns, and plundered the area.

**62** Gaza's men asked for terms. Jonathan gave his hand on it, took the rulers' sons as hostages, sent them to Jerusalem, and continued north to Damascus.

**63** Word came that Demetrius's commanders had arrived in Kedesh, in Galilee, with a large army — specifically targeting Jonathan.

**64** He went to meet them himself, leaving Simon to hold the country.

**65** Simon moved on Beth-zur, laying siege for many days until the garrison was pinned down.

**66** They sent out peace feelers. Simon accepted — then expelled them and took the city, putting in his own garrison.

**67** Jonathan and his army camped by the Sea of Galilee. At dawn they moved out toward the plain of Hazor.

**68** They walked into a trap. The enemy's main force came at them from the front while a hidden contingent burst out of the hills on their flanks.

**69** The ambush hit and Jonathan's entire force broke and ran —

**70** every single man, until only two officers were left standing: Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Chalphi.

**71** Jonathan tore his clothes, threw dirt on his head, and prayed.

**72** Then he turned and charged. The enemy broke and fled.

**73** When his own runaway soldiers saw what was happening, they turned around, rejoined him, and the whole force chased the enemy all the way back to their camp at Kedesh, where they made their own camp.

**74** About three thousand of the enemy fell that day. Jonathan went home to Jerusalem.
